items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 19...f5 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is f5, and Nf6 is within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 the engine rates this position between 0.3 and 1.5 pawns better for White.
A white pawn stands on e4.

hints: List the pawn breaks Black has. Which ones challenge White's centre?
Look for a pawn move that attacks White's e4 pawn.
items.explain: In a four-line search (the engine ranks its four best moves at once) at depth 16, the engine puts 19...f5 first. It is the game move; 19...Nf6 is within 0.4 of a pawn of it. At depth 16 the position is a little better for White, not winning: the engine rates it between 0.3 and 1.5 pawns for White. Evidence at a stated depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.h5f6: Also close to equal in engine terms; f5 is the game move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 21...Nf6 is legal.
21...Nf4 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Nf6.
At depth 16, 21...Nf4 is at least 50 centipawns below the top move.
After Nf4 two white pieces attack the knight.
After Nf4 two black pieces defend the knight.
One white piece attacks the knight on h5.
One black piece defends the knight on h5.

hints: First list which of your pieces are attacked and which are loose (attacked and not defended).
The knight on h5 is attacked once and defended once. Does it have to stay?
Compare a retreat of the knight with a move that puts it on a square White can capture.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16, the engine puts 21...Nf6 first. The game move 21...Nf4 puts the knight on a square attacked twice (by the g3 pawn and the bishop on e3) and defended twice, and at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 50 centipawns below Nf6. Tal's choice was a sacrifice, not the engine's first choice. Compare the numbers in the next board.

feedback_by_move.h5f4: This is the game move. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 50 centipawns below Nf6; see the numbers in the next board.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 23.a3 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is a3.
At depth 16, 23.Bd2 is at least 100 centipawns below the top move.
After a3 one white piece (the pawn) attacks the queen on b4.
The black queen stands on b4.
At depth 16 the engine rates this position between 0.8 and 2.5 pawns better for White.

hints: Look at Black's queen. What does it attack, and what can you do to it with tempo?
Which of your pawns can attack the queen?
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16, the engine puts 23.a3 first, attacking the queen on b4 with a pawn. The game move 23.Bd2 is at least 100 centipawns lower at depth 16: after it the engine rates the position near level, after 23.a3 clearly better for White. Evidence at a stated depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.e3d2: This is the game move. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 100 centipawns below a3.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 25.Bxf3 is legal.
25.Rxb2 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bxf3.
At depth 16, 25.Rxb2 is at least 400 centipawns below the top move.
The black queen stands on b2.
A black pawn stands on f3.

hints: Count what each side can capture, not only what you can capture.
Taking the queen is possible. Before you do, list every black capture that remains afterwards.
One of your bishop captures removes the black pawn on f3.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16, the engine puts 25.Bxf3 first. The game move 25.Rxb2 takes the queen but, at depth 16, is at least 400 centipawns below the top move. Taking the biggest piece is not the same as the best move.

feedback_by_move.b1b2: This is the game move: it wins the queen, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 400 centipawns below Bxf3.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 26...Rd4 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Rd4, and Be5+ is within a pawn of it.
At depth 16 the engine rates this position at least 3 pawns better for Black.
A black pawn stands on e2.

hints: Look at the rook on c4 and the white pieces near d4.
Which squares can the rook reach, and which of them can White capture on?
The rook goes to the d-file.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16, the engine puts 26...Rd4 first, with 26...Be5+ also strong (one of two strong moves). It is the game move. At depth 16 the engine rates the position at least 3 pawns better for Black. Evidence at a stated depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.g7e5: Also strong: the engine rates it clearly winning for Black. 26...Rd4 is the game move and the engine's first choice.
